title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and foot discomfort.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old man presenting for a routine evaluation of his type 2 diabetes mellitus and associated peripheral neuropathy. He reports occasional tingling and numbness in his toes but denies any acute fractures or open wounds. He maintains a consistent regimen of diet and exercise to manage his glucose levels. He states that his symptoms remain stable and have not worsened since the last visit.

Medication List
None.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals intact sensation to light touch in the bilateral feet, though some diminished sensation is noted in the distal toes. No ulcers or signs of infection are present. Skin is dry but intact.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes: Currently diet controlled.
2. Peripheral neuropathy: The patient’s neuropathy is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current lifestyle modifications focusing on diet and exercise. The patient will return in three months for a follow-up evaluation of his feet and glucose management.

Electronically signed, A. Rivera, NP, 05/12/2026
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
